beats.title: Merged After Extended Beta Validation
beats.body: The async chunk loading and generation feature was merged into master on September 26, 2018, after a multi-week public beta period where real production servers stress-tested the implementation. Key concurrency hazards — including unsafe entity additions during generation, lock contention on region saving, and non-thread-safe data converters — were resolved iteratively before merge. A custom priority-queue executor was built to minimize main-thread blocking while keeping generation operations world-local and single-threaded.

beats.title: Engineering Lessons
lessons: When integrating concurrency into a system not designed for it, isolate unsafe subsystems behind single-threaded executors rather than forcing full thread-safety everywhere at once.
Public beta testing with real production workloads surfaces concurrency bugs — like memory leaks under bulk generation — that synthetic tests rarely expose.
A priority-aware work queue lets you defer non-urgent work asynchronously while still meeting latency requirements when the main thread urgently needs a result.
